title: Poincare duality conventions
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite
extension $E/\Ql$ contained in a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$, with
valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an
integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. Put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a
smooth, separated finite-type, geometrically
connected $k_0$-scheme of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ (not
necessarily proper), put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, set $s=\Spec k$, and let
$a_X:X\to s$ be the structure morphism, assumed
exceptional-adjoint
admissible at every finite coefficient stage. On the
small pro-etale site of $X$,
use

$$
D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)\qquad(\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}),
$$

the bounded
constructible and finite-Tor
categories, the
derived pullback, tensor,
and internal Hom, the
derived direct image, the
compact-support direct image,
and the exceptional inverse
image, with the constructions and adjunctions of those definitions;
in particular

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda
$$

with $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, and the
ordinary and
compact-support cohomology are

$$
R\Gamma(X,K),\ \ R\Gamma_c(X,K),\ \ H^i(X,K),\ \ H_c^i(X,K).
$$

Use the coefficient twists
$K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda(m)$ and the
Frobenius normalization
on them ($q^{-m}$ on $\Lambda(m)$, $q^m$ on $\Lambda(-m)$). At the
point $s$, the finite
coefficient categories are $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$,
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, and the
common-stage category of
algebraically
closed coefficients; write $A$ for the coefficient ring of the point.
For $C$ in such a category put

$$
C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,A).
$$

The $F$-operators use the strict Weil structures of [def-pur-tate-datum].
Put $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$, the inverse of the field automorphism
$z\mapsto z^q$ of $k$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and write
$g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma):X\to X$.
For an object $(K,\varphi)$ with the specified strict Weil structure
$\varphi:Lg^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, use the following operators. With the ordinary and compact-support transports
$\tau_K$ and $\tau_{c,K}$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport], put
$$
 F_K=R\Gamma(X,\varphi)\circ\tau_K,
 \qquad
 F_{c,K}=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)\circ\tau_{c,K}.
$$
The transports are isomorphisms by
[lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso]. On $H^i$ and $H_c^i$ use the
induced maps $\mathrm H^i(F_K)$ and $\mathrm H^i(F_{c,K})$; the $r$-th
iterate, for $r\geq1$, means the $r$-fold composite of the corresponding
endomorphism. At $E$ coefficients these are exactly the global geometric
Frobenius operators of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. At finite
coefficients the displayed compact-support operator is the operator of
[def-trf-frobenius-operators], clause 1 at $m=1$. That its $r$-th iterate
is the composite of that clause at $m=r$, with the iterated Weil
isomorphism of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map], is the separate statement
[lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description]; it is not part of this
definition. The integral and
algebraically closed versions use respectively the compatible finite-stage
and common finite coefficient-field conventions of [def-pur-tate-datum]
and [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. The canonical orientation is the one
of the smooth
dualizing complex supplied by the purity chapter: at $\Lambda=A$ the
canonical isomorphism of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] for $f=a_X$,
and for $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ the canonical identification
of [cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes]: the canonical choice

$$
\eta_X:\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

For
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ put

$$
\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(K,\omega_{X,\Lambda}\bigr),
\qquad
K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(K,\Lambda_X\bigr),
$$

the *Verdier dual* and the *coefficient dual*.

Properness of $X_0$ is not part of this setting: the duality statements
formulated in it use compact supports $R\Gamma_c$ against ordinary
cohomology $R\Gamma$ and never compare the two. Properness is imposed
explicitly, and only, in the statements that need
$Ra_{X!}\cong Ra_{X*}$ (the untwisted trace on $H^{2d}$, the trace–cup
pairing on ordinary cohomology, and proper Poincare duality).

mathlib_searches.query: Poincare duality conventions pro-etale constructible finite Tor categories Tate twist and dualizing complex
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: AddChar.doubleDualEquiv, FGModuleCat.FGModuleCatDual, PiTensorProduct dual lemmas, CommRing.Pic.inv_eq_dual, and Algebra.Extension.tensorCotangentSpace. These concern different objects and do not give the convention package.
Twenty-five displayed hits: recurrence, PBW, and bibliographic mentions of Verdier or Verdier quotients; none is this definition.

mathlib_searches.query: Poincare duality conventions for constructible finite Tor pro-etale complexes with adic coefficients and canonical smooth purity orientation
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: etale/smooth loci, BDeRham(Plus), Kaehler differentials and standard smooth algebras. None defines this convention package.

Ten displayed hits in AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/{ElladicCohomology,Proetale}.lean. Read Proetale.lean lines 45-65 and ElladicCohomology.lean lines 30-95: these define a pro-etale topology, a continuous ell-adic coefficient sheaf, and its cohomology, not the six-operation/orientation convention package.

mathlib_searches.query: Verdier dual as derived internal Hom into the dualizing complex and coefficient dual as derived Hom into the coefficient ring on a scheme
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: LightCondensed internal Hom points, CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H/cohomologyPresheafFunctor, and Scheme global-sections maps. None supplies scheme dualizing complexes, exceptional inverse image, and the stated coefficient-stage conventions.

mathlib_searches.query: derived internal Hom duality for constructible complexes on the pro-etale site with Tate twists
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, all concerning LightCondensed internal Hom or monoidal closed structures on LightProfinite module sheaves. None states the scheme six-operation, four-coefficient-stage, Frobenius and orientation convention package.
Twenty-five displayed hits, concerning Verdier localization, bibliographic references and dualization of unrelated constructions; none states this convention package.

split_report.summary: Revalidated the returned definition split on the current DAG, including the changed statement of def-trf-frobenius-operators. Defined ordinary and compact-support Frobenius by typed cohomology-transport composites at all four coefficient stages; identified the finite compact-support operator with clause 1 at m=1 and used the existing iterated Weil-map definition for positive iterates. Retained every geometric and coefficient hypothesis and the canonical purity orientation. Reused existing constituent definitions and scalar/isomorphism theorems, with no new nodes, Mathlib leaves, or exact Lean attachment. This definition has no proof steps. The delivery tool rebases the split onto the current DAG; its required server preflight is rerun after the repair. Fresh second reading made the geometric field Frobenius and strict Weil map explicit, added the existing Frobenius-definition dependency, and independently repeated semantic and source searches. Maintainer reading: the orientation now cites the finite-stage theorem at A and the existing higher-stage identification cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes at O_E, E and Qlbar (the finite theorem is proved only at A); the finite-coefficient iterate comparison is cited to the existing lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description instead of being asserted inside the definition.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the setting, four coefficient categories, six operations, cohomology, twists and Frobenius normalization, canonical purity orientation, and the three dual definitions in literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-cor-sp-all-coefficients/def-pod-conventions.md. This is a definition, not the key theorem of its inherited unit, so there are no unit proof steps or realization fields to fill.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NY-c323e9847 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item against main-20261015 def-pod-conventions.md and its blueprint_update, plus the statement of every stmt_dep and the new candidates. Setting, hypotheses (including exceptional-adjoint admissibility), categories, operations, twists, the scalar from lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar, point and Verdier/coefficient duals, and the properness paragraph all match the source. The rewritten F-operator paragraph reads the source faithfully: F_K=RΓ(φ)∘τ_K and F_{c,K}=RΓ_c(φ)∘τ_{c,K} are typed endomorphisms by def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport and are isomorphisms by clause 3 of lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso; at E this is def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius, and at A it is clause 1 of def-trf-frobenius-operators at m=1. There are no new nodes and no proof steps. I made two repairs in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/def-pod-conventions.json. (1) C4/E4: η_X is used at all four coefficient stages, but thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object works only at Λ=A (its step 1, and def-pur-conventions). I now cite it at A and add the existing cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes for O_E, E and Q̄_ℓ. (2) The claim inside the definition that the finite-coefficient iterates equal the clause-1 composites at m=r was uncited; it is now cited to the existing lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description and marked as not part of the definition. Neither added dependency reaches the item, so there is no cycle. Not changed: the inherited chapter/unit binding mismatch is maintainer-owned. The source's admissibility hypothesis may be very restrictive in positive dimension, since the admissibility node's own warning says its FullCD clause fails for an elliptic curve; I kept it, because removing it would change the source's definition.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
